title: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling In Time Via Autonomous Quantum Error Correction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg scaling in time for parameter estimation, overcoming standard quantum limits.
motivation: Standard quantum metrology suffers from decoherence, limiting precision scaling to the standard quantum limit. The authors aim to achieve Heisenberg scaling in time by integrating error correction directly into the sensing protocol.
method: They propose an autonomous quantum error correction scheme using a bosonic code (e.g., cat code) that continuously corrects errors without active feedback, enabling the sensor to maintain coherence over extended times.
result: The scheme achieves Heisenberg scaling in time, i.e., the estimation precision scales as 1/T, where T is the total sensing time, even in the presence of noise.
conclusion: Autonomous quantum error correction provides a practical route to surpass the standard quantum limit in time-continuous metrology, with implications for quantum sensing and thermodynamics of information.

title: Louvre: Relaxing Hardware Requirements Of Quantum Ldpc Codes By Routing With Expanded Quantum Instruction Set
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a routing-based approach to relax hardware connectivity requirements for quantum LDPC codes using an expanded quantum instruction set.
motivation: Quantum LDPC codes promise low overhead but require high connectivity, which is challenging for near-term hardware. This work aims to reduce connectivity demands by introducing routing operations.
method: The authors design an expanded quantum instruction set that includes routing operations, enabling efficient mapping of LDPC code circuits onto hardware with limited connectivity. They analyze the trade-offs between routing overhead and code performance.
result: The proposed method significantly reduces the required hardware connectivity for implementing quantum LDPC codes, with modest increases in circuit depth and qubit overhead.
conclusion: Routing with an expanded instruction set is a practical approach to make quantum LDPC codes more feasible on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum network and error correction integration.

title: Three-outcome Multipartite Bell Inequalities: Applications To Dimension Witnessing And Spin-nematic Squeezing In Many-body Systems
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: Derives three-outcome multipartite Bell inequalities and applies them to dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
motivation: To develop Bell inequalities beyond the standard two-outcome case, enabling detection of nonlocality in systems with higher-dimensional measurements and applications to quantum information tasks.
method: Constructs Bell inequalities using three-outcome measurements, analyzes their violation in many-body spin systems, and connects to spin-nematic squeezing and dimension witnessing.
result: New families of Bell inequalities are derived, and their violation is shown to witness quantum dimensions and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
conclusion: Three-outcome Bell inequalities provide a useful tool for quantum information processing and characterization of many-body quantum states.

title: High-quality And Field Resilient Microwave Resonators On Ge Quantum Well Heterostructures
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-quality and field-resilient microwave resonators fabricated on germanium quantum well heterostructures, a key component for hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Ge quantum wells are a promising platform for hole spin qubits, but integrating high-performance microwave resonators is challenging due to material constraints and magnetic field sensitivity.
method: The authors design and fabricate superconducting microwave resonators on Ge/SiGe heterostructures, characterizing their internal quality factors and resilience to in-plane magnetic fields.
result: They achieve internal quality factors exceeding 10^5 at single-photon powers and demonstrate field resilience up to 1 T, with minimal degradation.
conclusion: These resonators are suitable for coupling to Ge hole spin qubits, enabling circuit QED experiments and advancing hybrid quantum systems with Ge-based qubits.

title: Demonstrating Optical Control Of Complex Phases In A Trapped-ion Qubit
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical control of complex phases in a trapped-ion qubit, enabling precise phase manipulation for quantum information processing.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but full control over qubit phases is essential for high-fidelity gates and algorithms. Optical control offers a pathway to faster and more coherent operations.
method: The authors use a combination of laser pulses to coherently control the phase of a trapped-ion qubit, leveraging the ion's internal and motional states. They characterize the phase evolution via Ramsey interferometry and process tomography.
result: They achieve high-fidelity phase control with low error rates, demonstrating the ability to implement arbitrary single-qubit phase gates. The method is robust against certain noise sources.
conclusion: Optical phase control is a viable technique for trapped-ion qubits, potentially improving gate fidelities and enabling more complex quantum algorithms.

title: Entanglement As A Fairness Mechanism In Randomized Quantum Games
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes using entanglement as a fairness mechanism in randomized quantum games, showing that entanglement can ensure fair outcomes in multi-party quantum games.
motivation: Classical randomization in games can be biased; quantum resources like entanglement may provide a way to enforce fairness without a trusted third party.
method: The authors design a quantum game protocol where entangled states are distributed among players, and measurements determine the game outcome; they analyze fairness conditions using quantum information theory.
result: They demonstrate that entanglement can guarantee fairness in certain classes of randomized quantum games, with security against cheating strategies.
conclusion: Entanglement serves as a resource for fairness in quantum games, opening new directions for quantum cryptography and multi-party computation.

title: An Almost-linear Time Decoding Algorithm For Quantum Ldpc Codes Under Circuit-level Noise
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: An almost-linear time decoding algorithm for quantum LDPC codes under circuit-level noise.
motivation: Efficient decoding of quantum LDPC codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing decoders are often too slow or assume simpler noise models.
method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm based on belief propagation with a novel scheduling and post-processing step that achieves almost-linear time complexity while handling circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm demonstrates high threshold and low logical error rates under circuit-level noise, with runtime scaling almost linearly with code length.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes that is both fast and effective under realistic noise, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Nanoscale Strain Wave Generation By A Piezoelectric Grating From Polar Vortices
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates the generation of nanoscale strain waves using a piezoelectric grating formed by polar vortices, enabling diffraction of X-rays.
motivation: To create a tunable diffraction grating for strain waves at the nanoscale, which could be used for probing and controlling material properties.
method: A periodic array of polar vortices in a ferroelectric material is modulated by an electric field via piezoelectric effect, generating a strain wave grating that diffracts X-rays.
result: The piezoelectric grating produces coherent nanoscale strain waves, as evidenced by X-ray diffraction patterns, with tunable periodicity and amplitude.
conclusion: Polar vortex structures can serve as reconfigurable diffraction gratings for strain waves, offering a new tool for nanoscale wave manipulation.

title: Towards Practical Quantum Neural Network Diagnostics With Neural Tangent Kernels
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses neural tangent kernels to diagnose and improve the training of quantum neural networks.
motivation: Quantum neural networks suffer from training issues like barren plateaus; the authors aim to provide a diagnostic tool to understand and mitigate these problems.
method: They apply neural tangent kernel theory to parameterized quantum circuits, analyzing the kernel's evolution during training to diagnose convergence and expressibility.
result: The method enables detection of barren plateaus and suggests adjustments to circuit architecture or initialization for better trainability.
conclusion: Neural tangent kernels offer a practical diagnostic framework for quantum neural networks, potentially improving their training and performance.

method: Experimental measurements on the kagome metal CsV3Sb5 using techniques sensitive to time-reversal symmetry breaking.
result: Signatures of spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking consistent with an imaginary charge density wave were observed.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence for a novel quantum state in kagome metals, advancing understanding of correlated electron systems.
